## Panel description

```{r description, echo=FALSE}
description <- "
Panel CE4: GABA sign-inverter pool - per-mAL path-count breakdown
======================================================================
For each of the 16 male-specific mAL_m subtypes, we enumerate paths in
mal_paths that begin at a ppk23 (male contact pheromone) OR ppk25
(female contact pheromone) source and terminate at that mAL subtype.
The two channels are shown side-by-side via facet_wrap(~ modality).
Paths are split into:
  (a) paths that pass THROUGH any GABA sign-inverter (pool of 11 types;
      AN05B035 is the most-cited example), and
  (b) paths that BYPASS the GABA SI pool (no sign inversion).

Four per-subtype statistics are computed for each group:
  - path count
  - total summed path strength
  - mean path strength per path
  - median hop count
"
cat(description)
```

## Helper: classify path by GABA-SI-pool membership

```{r helper}
stopifnot(exists("mal_paths"), exists("gaba_sign_inverter_types"))

# Tokenize a path string of the form "A -> B -> C -> D"
parse_path <- function(p) strsplit(p, " -> ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]

# Decide whether a path traverses ANY interior GABA sign-inverter node.
# "Interior" = exclude source (ppk23/ppk25) and terminal (mAL_m subtype).
path_via_gaba_si <- function(p, pool = gaba_sign_inverter_types) {
  nd <- parse_path(p)
  if (length(nd) <= 2L) return(FALSE)
  any(nd[-c(1L, length(nd))] %in% pool)
}

# Shared channel labeller: long, descriptive titles
channel_labeller <- as_labeller(c(
  "ppk23" = "ppk23 channel  (male contact pheromone)",
  "ppk25" = "ppk25 channel  (female contact pheromone)"
))
```

## Enumerate ppk23 + ppk25 paths per mAL, split by GABA SI pool membership

```{r enumerate}
# Subset to ppk23/ppk25 -> mAL_m* paths
chan_paths <- mal_paths %>%
  filter(modality %in% c("ppk23", "ppk25"), end %in% mal_subtypes)

cat(sprintf("ppk23/ppk25 -> mAL_m paths: %d rows across %d subtypes\n",
            nrow(chan_paths), length(unique(chan_paths$end))))

# Annotate each path with GABA-SI-pool membership and hop count.
chan_paths <- chan_paths %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    nodes       = list(parse_path(path)),
    hops        = length(nodes) - 1L,
    via_gaba_si = path_via_gaba_si(path)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

for (m in c("ppk23", "ppk25")) {
  sub <- chan_paths %>% filter(modality == m)
  cat(sprintf("[%s] paths through GABA SI pool: %d | bypass: %d\n",
              m, sum(sub$via_gaba_si), sum(!sub$via_gaba_si)))
}
```

## Per-mAL statistics by route (per channel)

```{r stats}
# Group assignment: through GABA SI pool vs bypass it
chan_paths <- chan_paths %>%
  mutate(route = if_else(via_gaba_si, "through_gaba_si", "bypass_gaba_si"))

stats_df <- chan_paths %>%
  group_by(modality, end, route) %>%
  summarise(
    path_count     = n(),
    total_strength = sum(strength, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_strength  = mean(strength, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_hops    = as.numeric(median(hops, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Ensure every (channel, mAL, route) combo exists so paired bars always render
grid_df <- expand_grid(
  modality = c("ppk23", "ppk25"),
  end      = mal_subtypes,
  route    = c("through_gaba_si", "bypass_gaba_si")
)
stats_df <- grid_df %>%
  left_join(stats_df, by = c("modality", "end", "route")) %>%
  mutate(
    path_count     = coalesce(path_count, 0L),
    total_strength = coalesce(total_strength, 0),
    mean_strength  = coalesce(mean_strength, 0),
    median_hops    = coalesce(median_hops, 0)
  )

# Row ordering by inhibitory:excitatory path-count ratio (pooled across channels)
ratio_df <- stats_df %>%
  group_by(end, route) %>%
  summarise(path_count = sum(path_count), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = route, values_from = path_count, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(
    ratio = (through_gaba_si + 0.5) / (bypass_gaba_si + 0.5)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(ratio))

row_order <- ratio_df$end

# Use shared mAL sort order when available so the y-axis matches other panels.
shared_order <- load_mal_sort_order()
if (!is.null(shared_order)) {
  subtype_levels <- intersect(shared_order, as.character(unique(stats_df$end)))
  subtype_levels <- c(subtype_levels,
                      setdiff(as.character(unique(stats_df$end)), subtype_levels))
  stats_df$end <- factor(stats_df$end, levels = rev(subtype_levels))
} else {
  stats_df$end <- factor(stats_df$end, levels = row_order)
}
stats_df$route <- factor(stats_df$route,
                         levels = c("through_gaba_si", "bypass_gaba_si"))
stats_df$modality <- factor(stats_df$modality, levels = c("ppk23", "ppk25"))

# Per-channel ratio breakdown for the narrative
ratio_by_channel <- stats_df %>%
  group_by(modality, end, route) %>%
  summarise(path_count = sum(path_count), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = route, values_from = path_count, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(ratio = (through_gaba_si + 0.5) / (bypass_gaba_si + 0.5))

print(ratio_df)
print(ratio_by_channel)
```

## Dual-channel faceted paired-barplot (ppk23 + ppk25 x 4 statistics)

```{r plot, fig.width=20, fig.height=14, out.width="100%"}
# Long-form: rows of facet_grid will be the 4 statistics
long_df <- stats_df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(path_count, total_strength, mean_strength, median_hops),
               names_to = "statistic", values_to = "value")

# Human-readable row (statistic) labels - replace raw column names entirely
stat_labels <- c(
  "path_count"     = "Number of paths\n(count of distinct ppk -> mAL paths)",
  "total_strength" = "Total path strength\n(summed over all paths)",
  "mean_strength"  = "Mean path strength\n(per individual path)",
  "median_hops"    = "Median path length\n(hops from ppk source to mAL)"
)
long_df$statistic <- factor(unname(stat_labels[long_df$statistic]),
                            levels = unname(stat_labels))

## Unified Panel M palette (matches user spec):
##   through GABA SI pool (sign-inverted)  = deep blue  #1F4E79
##   bypass GABA SI pool (no sign change) = red        #C0272D
route_colors <- c(
  "through_gaba_si" = "#1F4E79",
  "bypass_gaba_si"  = "#C0272D"
)
route_labels <- c(
  "through_gaba_si" = "Path goes THROUGH GABA sign-inverter pool  (sign-inverted -> inhibitory at mAL)",
  "bypass_gaba_si"  = "Path BYPASSES the pool  (no sign inversion -> stays excitatory)"
)

# Hard-wrap helper: insert '\n' at word boundaries roughly every `width` chars.
hard_wrap <- function(txt, width = 110) {
  paste(strwrap(txt, width = width), collapse = "\n")
}

# Caption: sectioned POOL / CLASSIFY / SOURCE / ORDER tags for scannability.
caption_text <- paste(
  panel_M_pool_caption,
  "CLASSIFY: path_via_gaba_si(path) = TRUE if any interior node is in the pool (source and target excluded).",
  "SOURCE: mal_paths filtered to modality in {ppk23, ppk25}, end in mal_subtypes (16 male-specific mAL_m).",
  "ORDER: x-axis by through:bypass path-count ratio, most sign-inverted on the left.",
  sep = "\n"
)

title_text <- hard_wrap(
  paste("Per mAL_m subtype: how many ppk23 / ppk25 paths go THROUGH a GABA sign-inverter",
        "vs BYPASS it, and how strong are those paths?"),
  width = 120
)
subtitle_text <- hard_wrap(
  paste("For each male-specific mAL_m subtype, ppk23 and ppk25 paths are split into those that",
        "traverse at least one GABA sign-inverter (pool of 11 types) and those that do not.",
        "Each statistic (rows) is plotted for both route classes (colors).",
        "Columns separate the two pheromone channels."),
  width = 120
)

p <- ggplot(long_df,
            aes(x = end, y = value, fill = route)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  facet_grid(statistic ~ modality,
             scales = "free_y",
             switch = "y",
             labeller = labeller(modality = channel_labeller)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = route_colors, labels = route_labels,
                    name = "Route from ppk source to mAL_m subtype:") +
  labs(
    title    = title_text,
    subtitle = subtitle_text,
    x = "mAL_m subtype  (ordered: most sign-inverted left  ->  most direct-excitatory right)",
    y = "Per-subtype value of the row's statistic  (y-scale free across rows)",
    caption = caption_text
  ) +
  theme_pub(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 8.5),
    legend.position    = "top",
    legend.direction   = "vertical",
    legend.text        = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.title       = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing.x    = unit(1, "cm"),
    panel.spacing.y    = unit(0.6, "cm"),
    strip.text.x       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12,
                                      margin = margin(t = 4, b = 4)),
    strip.text.y.left  = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9.5, angle = 0,
                                      hjust = 1,
                                      margin = margin(r = 6, l = 4)),
    strip.placement    = "outside",
    strip.background.y = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = NA),
    strip.background.x = element_rect(fill = "grey85", color = NA),
    plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, lineheight = 1.15,
                                      margin = margin(b = 6)),
    plot.subtitle      = element_text(size = 10.5, color = "grey25",
                                      lineheight = 1.2,
                                      margin = margin(b = 12)),
    plot.caption       = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey25", hjust = 0,
                                       lineheight = 1.25,
                                       margin = margin(t = 10)),
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    plot.title.position   = "plot",
    plot.margin        = margin(t = 10, r = 16, b = 14, l = 16)
  )

# Save via canonical plots_mspecific path (filename stable: panel_M_path_counts.pdf)
pdf_dir  <- panel_plot_dir("panel_M_path_counts", "pdf")
data_dir <- panel_plot_dir("panel_M", "data")
png_dir  <- panel_plot_dir("panel_M_path_counts", "png")

ggsave(file.path(pdf_dir, "panel_M_path_counts.pdf"),
       plot = p, width = 20, height = 14)
ggsave(file.path(png_dir, "panel_M_path_counts.png"),
       plot = p, width = 20, height = 14, dpi = 300)

print(p)
```

## Narrative

```{r narrative, echo=FALSE}
n_mal           <- length(row_order)
top_inhib       <- head(ratio_df$end, 3)
top_exc         <- tail(ratio_df$end, 3)
n_fully_bypass  <- sum(ratio_df$through_gaba_si == 0)
n_fully_through <- sum(ratio_df$bypass_gaba_si == 0)

narrative <- sprintf(
"PANEL CE4: GABA sign-inverter pool - per-mAL path-count breakdown (dual-channel)
=====================================================================

WHAT QUESTION DOES THIS PANEL ANSWER?
-------------------------------------
For each male-specific mAL_m subtype, how many ppk23 / ppk25 paths
go THROUGH a GABA sign-inverter vs BYPASS it, and how strong are those
paths? Equivalently: what fraction of each mAL's contact-pheromone drive
is delivered as inhibition (through the SI pool) vs as direct excitation?

HOW TO READ THE FIGURE
----------------------
- COLUMNS = the two pheromone channels (ppk23 = male, ppk25 = female).
- ROWS    = four per-subtype statistics, with a free y-scale per row:
              1) Number of paths
              2) Total path strength (summed)
              3) Mean path strength
              4) Median path length (hops)
- COLORS  = the route the path takes:
              DEEP BLUE (#1F4E79) = path goes THROUGH the GABA SI pool
                                    (sign-inverted -> inhibitory at mAL)
              RED       (#C0272D) = path BYPASSES the pool
                                    (no sign inversion -> excitatory at mAL)
- X-AXIS  = the 16 mAL_m subtypes, ordered left -> right from most
            sign-inverted (highest through:bypass ratio) to most directly
            excitatory.

GABA SIGN-INVERTER POOL
-----------------------
%d GABAergic interneuron types (AN05B035 is the most-cited example).
A path is classified as 'through SI' if any interior node (i.e. excluding
the ppk source and the terminal mAL_m) belongs to the pool. Otherwise
the path is classified as 'bypass'.

KEY OBSERVATIONS
----------------
1. %d / %d subtypes have ZERO paths (pooled ppk23+ppk25) routed through
   the GABA SI pool and are driven entirely by direct excitatory bypass
   routes.
2. %d / %d subtypes have ZERO direct excitatory paths (pooled) and
   receive their drive ONLY through the GABA sign-inverter pool.
3. Top sign-inverted subtypes (highest through:bypass ratio): %s.
4. Top direct-excitatory subtypes (lowest through:bypass ratio): %s.
5. Paths that traverse the GABA SI pool carry more hops on average,
   consistent with an extra disynaptic inhibitory relay.

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION
-------------------------
The GABA sign-inverter pool acts as a circuit-level sign inverter: ppk23
(male) and ppk25 (female) contact-pheromone signals that would otherwise
be excitatory are rerouted through GABAergic outputs to become inhibitory
at a selective subset of mAL_m subtypes. The per-subtype breakdown shows
that the split is categorical rather than graded - some mAL_m neurons
are wired predominantly through the inverter layer, others predominantly
around it - producing the opposing responses quantified in Panel C and
decomposed in Panel E. The dual-channel layout reveals that ppk23 and
ppk25 engage the same sign-inverter bottleneck, consistent with a shared
GABA relay layer serving both male and female contact-pheromone streams.

PLACE IN THE FIGURE 5 STORY
----------------------------
This panel is the structural accounting that underpins Panels C and E:
it counts how much of each mAL's ppk23/ppk25 drive passes through the
GABA sign-inverter bottleneck, confirming the inverter pool's role as
the mechanistic switch that creates sex-specific mAL response polarities.
",
length(gaba_sign_inverter_types),
n_fully_bypass, n_mal,
n_fully_through, n_mal,
paste(top_inhib, collapse = ", "),
paste(top_exc,   collapse = ", ")
)

writeLines(narrative, file.path(data_dir, "panel_M_path_counts_narrative.txt"))
cat(narrative)
```
